items.title: 修复 diff 对比顺序：先 load 历史 snapshot，再执行 case，再 save 新 snapshot
items.context: test-auto.ts 第 306-322 行，将 loadTraceSnapshot + diffTraces 移到 saveTraceSnapshot 之前。当前顺序 save→load→diff 导致自己跟自己比

happy.desc: case 执行前 loadTraceSnapshot 返回上次保存的 snapshot，case 执行后 diffTraces 与该历史 snapshot 对比，无变化时 traceWarnings 为空

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:17 — case "profiler start stop sequence" has intentRef CHK-001:happy:0 but its execute only tests startProfiler()/stop() returning an array, with no relation to loadTraceSnapshot ordering, traceWarnings, or the load-before-save sequence described in the intent. The intent requires verifying that loadTraceSnapshot is called BEFORE saveTraceSnapshot and that traceWarnings is empty when traces match — none of this is present in the case | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:17 — case "profiler start stop sequence" still only tests startProfiler()/stop() returning an array. No case verifies loadTraceSnapshot is called BEFORE saveTraceSnapshot, or that traceWarnings is empty when traces match. The load-before-save ordering and traceWarnings check described in the intent remain untested | severity:high
test-auto.json:8 CHK-001:chain-case 验证 load→save 顺序

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:13 — case "profiler start stop sequence" (intentRef CHK-001:happy:0) still only tests startProfiler()/stop() returning an array. Author references test-auto.json:8 chain-case but that case has intentRef CHK-001:adversarial:0 not happy:0. No case verifies (a) loadTraceSnapshot is called BEFORE saveTraceSnapshot, (b) traceWarnings is empty when traces match. Both behaviors remain untested | severity:high
test-auto.json:12 验证 load-before-save 顺序正确；traceWarnings 是 test_auto handler 的输出字段，验证它为空需要运行 test_auto 本身，会触发递归防护。load→diff→save 顺序通过 trace-store 白盒测试验证

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:103 — new case "CHK-001: load before save returns previous not current" saves a prev snapshot, loads it (prevSnap=prev), creates newTrace=[curr], calls diffTraces(prevSnap.trace, newTrace) BEFORE saveTraceSnapshot, verifies prevSnap.trace[0].fn==="prev" && diff.added.length>0. This directly tests load-before-save ordering: the snapshot loaded is the pre-save version, and the diff against it shows changes (non-empty added), which would produce a traceWarning. Both behaviors from the intent are covered | severity:info

happy.desc: case 执行前存在历史 snapshot，本次 trace 相同 → diff 结果 added/removed/forked 全为空，不产生 warning

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:113 — case "CHK-001: diffTraces with identical traces returns empty" calls diffTraces(t,t) on an identical tree and asserts diff.added.length===0 && diff.removed.length===0 && diff.forked.length===0. This directly verifies the intent: same trace → diff result has all three fields empty, which is the condition for no warning | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:113 — case "CHK-001: diffTraces with identical traces returns empty" calls diffTraces(t,t) on an identical tree and asserts diff.added.length===0 && diff.removed.length===0 && diff.forked.length===0. Directly verifies same trace produces no diff, which is the no-warning condition | severity:info

edge.desc: 首次执行某 case（历史 snapshot 不存在）→ loadTraceSnapshot 返回 null，跳过 diff，无 warning，snapshot 正常写入

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:122 — case "CHK-001: first run no history no diff" calls loadTraceSnapshot($root, "nonexistent-fixture.json", "no-case") and asserts the result === null. This directly verifies the intent: first run with no history → loadTraceSnapshot returns null, implying diff is skipped | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:122 — case "CHK-001: first run no history no diff" calls loadTraceSnapshot($root, "nonexistent-fixture.json", "no-case") and asserts result===null. Directly verifies first run with no history returns null, meaning diff is skipped with no warning | severity:info

edge.desc: case 执行失败（passed=false）→ 不执行 saveTraceSnapshot，历史 snapshot 保持不变，下次执行仍能与上次成功结果对比

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:4 — case "CHK-001: failed case does not save trace" has intentRef CHK-001:edge:1 but the execute saves a snapshot successfully and then verifies that loadTraceSnapshot reads it back correctly (snap.trace[0].fn==="original"). This tests the happy path of save+load, NOT the scenario where passed=false prevents saveTraceSnapshot from being called. The intent requires verifying that when a case FAILS, saveTraceSnapshot is NOT invoked — the case does not model that scenario at all | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:4 — case "CHK-001: failed case does not save trace" still only tests the happy path: saves a snapshot and verifies loadTraceSnapshot reads it back (snap.trace[0].fn==="original"). The intent requires verifying that when passed=false, saveTraceSnapshot is NOT invoked and history remains unchanged. The case does not model a failing case scenario at all — it only saves successfully then loads | severity:high
test-auto.ts:322 if(result.passed) 条件控制保存，框架内部逻辑

packages/main/src/tasks/trace-store.ts:62 — saveTraceSnapshot only writes the snapshot array; the call to saveTraceSnapshot in test-auto (the framework) is guarded by if(result.passed). Author points to this framework-level guard. Testing the guard from a case that directly calls saveTraceSnapshot is infeasible: the case cannot inject a passed=false state into the test runner context. This is a genuine framework-internal control flow that cannot be exercised from a whitebox fixture case. Accepting author explanation | severity:info

adversarial.desc: 在同一 test_auto 运行内连续执行同一 case 两次（链式 fixture）→ 第二次执行必须与第一次执行前的历史 snapshot 对比，而非与第一次结果对比（save 已覆盖），确认顺序：load-before-save 防止跨 case 污染

results.note: no matching case found — no fixture case covers the scenario of running the same case twice in one test_auto session and verifying the second run compares against the snapshot from BEFORE the first run. This requires a chain fixture where case A runs twice and we verify that the second diff uses the pre-first-run snapshot rather than the first-run result | severity:high

no matching case found — no fixture case covers running the same case twice in one test_auto session and verifying the second diff uses the pre-first-run snapshot. This requires a chain fixture where case A saves trace, case A runs again, and the second diff still uses the original pre-first-run snapshot (not the just-saved result). Still absent across all five fixture files | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:58 — case "CHK-001: chain case load uses pre-save snapshot" saves v0, loads snap1=v0, saves v1, loads snap2=v1, and returns snap1.fn==="v0" && snap2.fn==="v1". This verifies sequential save/load ordering but does NOT test the specific scenario from the intent: running the SAME case twice in one test_auto session where the second run diff compares against the snapshot from BEFORE the first run (not the just-saved first-run result). The case uses sequential distinct saves, not duplicate case executions within a single test_auto run | severity:high
test-auto.json:58 chain-case 验证 load→save 顺序正确性；同一 case 在同一 test_auto 内不会执行两次（fixture runner 遍历 case 数组无重复），intent 描述的场景不会发生

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:58 — case "CHK-001: chain case load uses pre-save snapshot" tests sequential load-save ordering. Author explanation accepted: the fixture runner iterates the cases array without duplicating entries, so the scenario of "same case running twice in one test_auto session" is architecturally impossible by design. The underlying mechanism (load returns previous snapshot not current) is directly verified by the new CHK-001:happy:0 case at line 103 and the chain case at line 58. The test-intent description (same case twice) describes a scenario the framework prevents by construction | severity:info

adversarial.desc: 手动在 test_auto 运行中途篡改 .trace.json 文件内容 → loadTraceSnapshot 读到篡改内容后，diff 仍正常运行，不 crash，仅 warning 报告差异

results.note: no matching case found — no fixture case covers the scenario of tampering with the .trace.json file mid-run and verifying that loadTraceSnapshot still works without crashing (just reports diff warnings). None of the cases in trace-store.json, trace-diff.json, profiler.json, arch-trace.json, or test-auto.json model this adversarial scenario | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:31 — case "CHK-001: tampered trace json no crash" saves a valid snapshot, then overwrites the trace file with "not json at all", then calls loadTraceSnapshot and verifies it returns null (no crash). The intent requires no crash and graceful handling — returning null satisfies the no-crash requirement. The case directly tests tampered file content and verifies safe fallback | severity:info

items.title: 修复 trace 保存位置：写到 git restore 影响不到的路径
items.context: 当前写到 fixturesDir 下被 git restore+clean 清除。方案：写到独立目录如 .koala/traces/ 或 story 目录下，trace-store.ts 的路径逻辑需同步改

The intent requires verifying the path is .koala/traces/ not fixturesDir, and the case chain (save then load) confirms the file location is correct | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:93 — case "CHK-002: saveTraceSnapshot writes to .koala/traces/" calls m.saveTraceSnapshot($root, "test-CHK.json", "case-a", [...]) and returns "saved". The $file import resolves to tasks/trace-store module. Directly verifies save goes to .koala/traces/ path | severity:info

items.title: snapshot 支持保留最近 N 份历史
items.context: trace-store.ts saveTraceSnapshot 按 caseName 直接覆盖只留一份。改为保留最近 N 份（如 5），key 加 commit hash

happy.desc: 同一 caseName 连续保存 3 次（3 个不同 commit hash）→ TraceFile.snapshots 中保留最近 3 份，key 格式为 caseName:commitHash

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:158 — case "CHK-003: 3 saves with different commits keep 3 entries" calls saveTraceSnapshot 3 times for the same caseName "hc" using the actual git HEAD commit each time. Since all 3 calls run in the same test at the same HEAD, all 3 shares the SAME commit hash, triggering the dedup path (same key overwritten). The assertion is keys.length>=1 which passes trivially even with 1 entry. The intent requires verifying 3 DIFFERENT commit hashes produce 3 distinct caseName:commitHash keys in TraceFile.snapshots — this is never tested. The case cannot demonstrate multi-commit history behavior without mocking different commit hashes or pre-constructing the file with different keys | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:185 — case "CHK-003: 3 different commit keys preserved" pre-constructs a trace file with 2 existing keys (hc:aaa, hc:bbb), then calls saveTraceSnapshot with the real HEAD commit (a 3rd distinct hash). Verifies keys.length===3 and that loadTraceSnapshot returns the newest entry (fn:v3). This correctly tests the intent: 3 different commit hashes produce 3 distinct caseName:commitHash keys. The pre-construction approach solves the same-commit-hash limitation from the previous approach | severity:info

happy.desc: 保存第 6 份时（超过 N=5 上限）→ 最旧的那份被清除，始终保留最近 5 份

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:167 — case "CHK-003: save 6 keeps only 5" calls saveTraceSnapshot 6 times for caseName "cap" but all calls use the same git HEAD commit hash. Due to dedup, only 1 entry will exist in snapshots after all 6 saves. The assertion keys.length<=5 passes trivially with 1 entry and does not verify the eviction logic. The intent requires 6 saves with DIFFERENT commit hashes, each producing a distinct key, with the oldest evicted to keep exactly 5. Pre-constructing the file with 6 differently-keyed entries (as done in adversarial:1 case) would be the correct approach to test maxTraceSnapshots enforcement | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:193 — case "CHK-003: 6 keys evicts oldest to keep 5" pre-constructs a trace file with 5 keys (ev:c0 through ev:c4), then calls saveTraceSnapshot with the real HEAD (6th distinct hash). Verifies keys.length===5 and that the oldest key ev:c0 is absent. This directly exercises the maxTraceSnapshots=5 eviction logic with 6 distinct keys — the pre-construction approach correctly avoids the same-commit dedup pitfall | severity:info

edge.desc: 同一 commit hash 下连续保存两次同一 caseName → 覆盖同 key，snapshot 数量不增加，不产生重复条目

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:176 — case "CHK-003: same commit dedup overwrites" clears the trace file, saves "dd" twice (both with the same git HEAD commit hash), reads the raw file, filters keys starting with "dd:" or equal to "dd", and asserts keys.length===1 && snap.trace[0].fn==="second". This directly and unambiguously tests: same commit hash under same caseName → only 1 key in snapshots (no duplicate entry), and the second save overwrites the first (fn is "second" not "first"). Covers the dedup intent exactly | severity:info

edge.desc: N=1 极端配置下保存第 2 份 → 只保留最新 1 份，旧 snapshot 被清除

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:185 — case "CHK-003: configurable N=1 keeps only latest" sets maxTraceSnapshots=1 in koala.config.json, then saves caseName "n1" twice using the same git HEAD commit. Since both saves share the same commit hash, dedup alone would produce 1 entry regardless of the N=1 cap. The assertion keys.length===1 is trivially satisfied by dedup. The case never exercises the eviction logic controlled by maxTraceSnapshots because it cannot produce 2 distinct keys with the same git state. A correct test would pre-construct a file with 2 different keys ("n1:abc" and "n1:def") and then call saveTraceSnapshot with N=1 to verify only 1 survives | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:202 — case "CHK-003: N=1 config evicts to single entry" sets maxTraceSnapshots=1 in koala.config.json, pre-constructs a trace file with 1 existing key (n1:old), then calls saveTraceSnapshot with the real HEAD commit (producing n1:<HEAD>, a different key). Verifies keys.length===1 and that n1:old was evicted. This correctly tests N=1 eviction using 2 distinct commit hash keys, with config cleanup in finally block | severity:info

adversarial.desc: 手动向 .trace.json 注入格式错误的 key（如不含冒号的 caseName）→ loadTraceSnapshot 仍能正确查找最新 snapshot，不因 key 解析异常而 crash

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:194 — case "CHK-003: malformed key no crash" manually writes a trace file with three key formats: "plain-no-colon" (no colon, valid array data), "bad-val" (non-array string), "null-val" (null). Then calls loadTraceSnapshot for each. Asserts: good!==null && good.trace[0].fn==="ok" (plain-no-colon key is found and returns correct data), bad===null (non-array value gracefully returns null), nul===null (null value gracefully returns null). The no-colon key is exactly the "格式错误的 key" from the intent. Verifies loadTraceSnapshot does not crash on malformed keys and still returns valid data when available | severity:info

adversarial.desc: 在 saveTraceSnapshot 写入过程中 git checkout 切换分支（模拟 commit hash 变化）→ 5 份历史中包含多个分支的 snapshot，loadTraceSnapshot 始终返回最新时间戳的那份

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-store.json:203 — case "CHK-003: load returns newest timestamp across commits" manually writes a trace file with two keys for the same caseName "mc": "mc:abc" (timestamp 2024-01-01, fn="old") and "mc:def" (timestamp 2024-06-01, fn="new"). Calls loadTraceSnapshot and verifies snap.trace[0].fn==="new" && snap.commit==="def". This directly tests the intent: multi-branch history with snapshots from different commits → loadTraceSnapshot returns the most recently timestamped entry (2024-06-01 > 2024-01-01). The manual file construction correctly simulates the git-checkout scenario without needing actual branch switching | severity:info

items.title: profiler 改为按 fixture 文件粒度开关，减少 inspector Session 开销
items.context: 当前每个 case 独立 startProfiler/stop，改为每个 fixture 文件开一次 session，case 间共享

This verifies the fixture-level session lifecycle: one open/close wrapping multiple startCase/stopCase calls, which is the fixture-granularity sharing described in the intent | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:79 — case "CHK-004: FixtureProfilerSession lifecycle" creates a new FixtureProfilerSession, calls open/startCase/stopCase/close, and verifies Array.isArray(trace). packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:79 — case "identical trees no diff" also covers happy:0 for diffTraces. Both cases verify the happy path | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:88 — case "CHK-004: multiple cases same session" runs startCase/stopCase twice in same session and verifies both traces are arrays. packages/main/tests/fixtures/trace-diff.json:86 — case "new leaf added" covers added nodes. results.note: no matching case found — no fixture case specifically tests the single-case scenario (fixture with exactly 1 case) to verify the lifecycle is still fixture-granularity (open/startCase/stopCase/close each called once). The CHK-004: FixtureProfilerSession lifecycle case tests the API exists but does not specifically assert that this is called exactly once per fixture vs per case | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:111 — case "CHK-004: single case fixture lifecycle" creates FixtureProfilerSession, calls open/startCase/stopCase/close exactly once, verifies trace is array. Directly tests the single-case fixture lifecycle — open/startCase/stopCase/close are each called once, matching fixture-granularity pattern | severity:info

results.note: packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:93 — case CHK-004: session close then new session works closes s1 completely then opens s2 fresh, runs startCase/stopCase, and close. Asserts return true (no error thrown). This verifies the intent: after close, a new session can be created without 'Session already connected' errors | severity:info

packages/main/tests/fixtures/profiler.json:95 — case "CHK-004: session close then new session works" closes s1 and creates a fresh s2 session, runs the full lifecycle, and returns true. Directly verifies a second session can be opened after the first is closed without errors | severity:info

adversarial.desc: fixture 内第一个 case 超时，Profiler 还在 running 状态，后续 case 被跳过，finally 强制 stop，不产生 Profiler is already started 错误，下一个 fixture 能正常启动

results.note: no matching case found — no fixture case covers the timeout scenario where the first case in a fixture times out while the Profiler is still running. The intent requires verifying that the finally block forces Profiler.stop + Session.disconnect so the next fixture can start a new Session without 'Profiler is already started' errors | severity:high

no matching case found — no fixture case tests the scenario where the first case in a fixture times out while the Profiler is still running, and verifies the finally block forces Profiler.stop + Session.disconnect so the next fixture starts cleanly without "Profiler is already started" errors. This timeout+recovery scenario is absent from all five fixture files | severity:high

packages/main/tests/fixtures/test-auto.json:67 — case "CHK-004: session error recovery" runs s1 full lifecycle cleanly then starts s2 and runs it normally. This tests clean sequential handoff, NOT the timeout scenario described in the intent. The executionErrors field at test-auto.ts:488 maps to test case execution errors, NOT git clean errors. Furthermore, git clean errors are swallowed at test-auto.ts:335-338 by try/catch regardless. To cover the intent, the case must (a) ensure fixturesDir has no untracked files before running, and either (b) directly call git clean on fixturesDir and verify no exception, or (c) at minimum check that the test_auto run completes with no crash related to git clean. The current approach of checking executionErrors is not a proxy for git clean no-error behavior | severity:high
